text: An object is released from rest from the top of a building of height $h$. Air resistance is negligible. What is the speed of the object immediately before striking the ground?
solution: B — Using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$ and $s = h \implies v = \sqrt{2gh}$.

text:
A rescue package is dropped horizontally from an aircraft at speed $u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from a height $h = 45\text{ m}$.

(a) Show that the time of flight is approximately $3.0\text{ s}$. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector upon impact. [3 marks]
solution:
(a) $t = \sqrt{2h/g} = \sqrt{90/9.81} \approx 3.03\text{ s}$.
(b) $v_y = gt = 9.81(3.03) = 29.7\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Total velocity $v = \sqrt{25^2 + 29.7^2} \approx 38.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

text: A block of mass $m$ rests on a rough horizontal surface. A horizontal force $F$ is applied, but the block remains stationary. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting on the block?
solution: C — Since the block remains at rest (static equilibrium), the net horizontal force is zero: $f_s = F$.

text: An ideal gas is held inside a sealed container of fixed volume $V$. The absolute temperature of the gas is doubled from $T$ to $2T$. What happens to the root-mean-square speed, $v_{\text{rms}}$, of the gas molecules?
choices: It increases by a factor of $\sqrt{2}$
solution: B — The average kinetic energy per molecule is $\frac{1}{2}m v_{\text{rms}}^2 = \frac{3}{2}k_B T \implies v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}$. Doubling absolute temperature increases speed by a factor of $\sqrt{2}$.

text:
A mass-spring oscillator executes simple harmonic motion along a horizontal surface with amplitude $A = 0.080\text{ m}$ and angular frequency $\omega = 12\text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

(a) Calculate the maximum acceleration $a_{\text{max}}$ experienced by the oscillating mass. [2 marks]
(b) Determine the speed of the mass when its displacement from equilibrium is $x = 0.050\text{ m}$. [2 marks]

A satellite orbits a planet of mass $M$ in a circular path of radius $r$ with orbital period $T$.

(a) Derive an expression for $T^2$ in terms of $G, M,$ and $r$. [3 marks]
(b) Explain why the gravitational force does no work on the satellite during this circular motion. [3 marks]
solution:
(a) Centripetal force equals gravitational force: $\frac{GMm}{r^2} = m\left(\frac{2\pi}{T}\right)^2 r \implies T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2 r^3}{GM}$.
(b) Gravitational force is perpendicular to instantaneous displacement ($F \perp v$), so $W = Fd\cos 90^\circ = 0$.

text: A positively charged particle with charge $+q$ moves with constant speed $v$ into a uniform magnetic field $B$ directed perpendicular into the page. Which path describes the initial motion of the particle?
choices: It deflects upwards following a parabolic trajectory
It deflects upwards following a circular arc
It deflects downwards following a circular arc
It continues in a straight line with increasing speed
solution: B — By the right-hand rule, $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ provides a centripetal force directed upwards, resulting in a circular arc.

text:
A sample contains $N_0 = 4.8 \times 10^{18}$ nuclei of a radioactive isotope with a half-life of $T_{1/2} = 6.0\text{ hours}$.

(a) Show that the decay constant $\lambda$ of this isotope is approximately $3.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ s}^{-1}$. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the initial activity $A_0$ of the sample in becquerels (Bq). [2 marks]
(c) State the number of undecayed nuclei remaining after $24\text{ hours}$. [1 mark]
solution:
(a) $\lambda = \frac{\ln 2}{T_{1/2}} = \frac{0.693}{21600\text{ s}} \approx 3.21 \times 10^{-5}\text{ s}^{-1}$.
(b) $A_0 = \lambda N_0 = 3.21 \times 10^{-5} \times 4.8 \times 10^{18} \approx 1.54 \times 10^{14}\text{ Bq}$.
(c) $24\text{ hours} = 4\text{ half-lives} \implies N = \frac{N_0}{2^4} = 3.0 \times 10^{17}$.
